newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile cenbank sees growth slowing in May and June.
newsitem.headline: Chile cenbank sees growth slowing in May and June.

text.p: Chile's economic growth should be less in May and June than the strong 6.5 percent recorded in April, said Central Bank president Carlos Massad.
"We don't believe that in the next two months there will be a repeat of the results seen in April," Massad told reporters.
"But without doubt the economy is already reflecting the recovery expected in the second quarter compared with what happened in the first quarter."
The official Imacec index released Monday showed growth picking up to 6.5 percent in April from 3.4 percent recorded in February and March.
"We don't have a figure (for May and June) but it will certainly be somewhat less than in April," said Massad.
Chilean financial markets reacted negatively to news of the strong April growth as investors feared it would delay a further cut in interest rates by the bank.
April's figure, which was higher than many analysts had been expecting, was the result of a high number of working days in the month and the heating up of the economy, he said.
Asked about the impact of the data on the bank's restrictive monetary policy, Massad replied:
"We don't think that the April figure is the one we should expect permanently in the next few months. It doesn't delay or bring forward a cut in (interest) rates."
